headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to pull U.S. troops from hostilities against Iran unless Congress approved them.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from fighting within or against Iran. That requirement would have applied unless Congress first passed a declaration of war or a law authorizing military force for that purpose. It would not have stopped the United States from defending itself, its personnel, or its facilities in other countries against an attack. On May 13, 2026, the Senate refused to take it up or end debate on it, so it did not pass.

who_it_affects.how: Troops taking part in hostilities against Iran would have been withdrawn unless Congress authorized the action.
The President would have needed approval from Congress before keeping U.S. forces in hostilities against Iran, except to defend against attacks.
Congress would have had to vote on a declaration of war or use-of-force authorization for U.S. military action against Iran to continue.
